title: 영어브리핑_2026-10-29
korean_summary: 내일 핵심: 아침에 Lency에게 0018 적입 시각 확인 → 오후 현장 참석, 원사 미신고 표 정오까지 받아 법인장 보고, Mai 항공 견적(11/10 출발) 11시 확인 후 선택
paragraphs: Part one. Opening.
Good morning, Anthony. Today is Thursday, October twenty-ninth. You have a busy day, but it is a clear one. Relax your shoulders and listen slowly.

This briefing has eight parts. Part one is this opening. Part two is the top three jobs for today. Part three is the reports you need to collect. Part four is the replies you owe. Part five is your schedule and deadlines for the next three days. Part six is English review. Part seven is a short role-play. Part eight is the closing.
When you hear a pause, say the sentence out loud. Let's begin.
Part two. Top three for today.
Number one. The Vince air shipment, SO six three four, twenty-six ten, zero zero one eight.
This is the shipment of six hundred fifteen pieces in two big hanger boxes. You plan to join the box loading on site.

Here is what happened yesterday. The two boxes arrived at the factory at ten a.m. So the boxes are ready. But the garments were not ready. One style had a broken stitch problem. The buyer asked for a one hundred percent check and a stretch test.

Lency replied yesterday morning. She said QA would finish the pulling test by noon. Then the packing team must repack one hundred eighty-six pieces. She also explained the five piece difference. The order is one hundred eighty-one pieces, and there are five pieces of over-shipment.
The most important line from Lency is this. They plan to start hanging the garments into the boxes this afternoon, Thursday.

Why does this matter? The truck leaves on Saturday at eight a.m. The airport cut-off is Saturday at four p.m. Hecny submitted the booking for a flight on November first. But the airline has not approved it yet. So there is no booking confirmation.
If loading slips to Friday, there is very little room left.

Your first action this morning is simple. Ask Lency for the final test result and the exact loading start time. Then ask Trinh Do to chase Hecny for the booking confirmation. Then block the time in your calendar and go to the floor.
Number two. The thread without customs declaration.
This is the thread from COATS PHONG PHU for Aritzia orders. The invoices were in the name of Poongin Trading, so PIDN did not declare the import.
You asked Trinh Do for a table. It should show the invoice number, the date received, the quantity, the amount, and the current stock. As of yesterday afternoon, there was no table in your email.
Why does it matter? The fabric and thread count is on Saturday. Head office will also check the customs balance. Mr Moon needs to decide how to handle this before then.
Your first action is to talk to Trinh Do face to face in the morning. Ask for the table by noon. Then report to Mr Moon with a clear proposal before you leave today.
Number three. The flight for Mr Asanka, our new sewing manager.
The plan changed yesterday. You told Mr Channa that the visa can be ready for entry on November seventh. Mr Channa replied that he will make the schedule for November tenth.
So you asked Mai for new flight quotes. Colombo to Da Nang, one way, on November tenth. Two or three cheap options, with the baggage weight for each. The deadline is today at eleven a.m.
Why does it matter? The ticket gets more expensive every day. Also, the sewing department has no manager after Mr Chamin leaves on October thirty-first. Mr Moon will want to know who covers the gap.
Your first action is to check Mai's quotes at eleven. Pick one option. Report it to Mr Moon with the plan for the gap. Then ask Mai to raise the purchase request.
Part three. Reports to collect.

First, Mai. She owes you two things today. One is the flight quotes at eleven. The other is the consumables ledger. She must enter all her imports and exports after October thirteenth by today. Mai often goes quiet, so check the file yourself, not only her reply.
Here is a sentence you can use.
Mai, just a reminder that the ledger update is due today. Please reply to me once it is done.

Second, Trinh Do. Before the Saturday count, she must fill in the receipt dates in the EXIM checklist. The deadline is today. Also, Lucy Lim from head office sent a third reminder yesterday. She wants the logistics cost chart for January to June in the new V4 format by October thirty-first.
Here is a sentence for Trinh.
Trinh, could you confirm whether the checklist and the V4 chart will be ready on time?

Third, Mint in the fabric warehouse. She must check racks seven and eight. She must also separate the interlining stock and explain the fabric with no rack location. Yesterday Hien updated the lot numbers. Fabric with no location is in red text. Fabric with no lot in the packing list is in yellow. Mint will update those later.
Here is a sentence for Mint.
Mint, please update the red and yellow lines in Hien's file before Saturday's count.

Fourth, Quan in IT. Yesterday he checked the monitor sizes and corrected six model names. You replied with the SSD plan. Thirteen SSDs at fifty percent health or lower will be replaced in three rounds. Quan now needs to get one quotation.
Here is a sentence for Quan.
Quan, please send me the SSD quotation and the expected delivery date.

Fifth, An in compliance. The investment registration certificate still has no issue date. So An suggests a new step. The supplier will send the environmental registration file to Lien Chieu Ward early for review. Then we will have proof that we started the process.
Here is a sentence for An.
An, please let me know when the supplier will submit the file to the Ward.
Part four. Replies I owe.

First, the overtime request for next week, November second to seventh. The production planning office sent a revised file yesterday morning to Mr Moon and to you. They are waiting for your review and approval. Check the hours against the legal limit before you say yes.
A first line could be this.
Thank you for the revised plan. I checked the hours, and I have one question before I approve.
Second, Hoang in HR sent the short-term worker payroll for October. Payment is on November third. Check the file today, so the accounting team has time on Friday and Saturday.
A first line could be this.
Hoang, I reviewed the short-term payroll file. Please check the two points below before payment.

Third, Mr Moon and the basic workers. He told you to keep the two button workers under Basic Worker, not Iron. You already updated the file. But he also asked you to check what each basic worker actually does and keep a record. He thinks head office may ask why the finishing team is over its target headcount.
Ask Ly or the packing leader for a short list today. Name, real task, and hours.
Fourth, An's environmental permit plan. She is waiting for your answer. A first line could be this.
An, I agree with submitting the file early. Please keep the receipt as evidence.
Part five. Schedule and deadlines.

Today, Thursday. Box loading for the Vince air shipment in the afternoon. Mai's flight quotes at eleven. Mai's ledger and Trinh's checklist are due today. Aritzia also has a final inspection by ITS today, but the merchandising team handles it. There is a barcode problem on some orders, so just watch the email.
Your calendar still shows "next week overtime report" on Thursdays. That job stopped on October fifteenth. You can delete it.

Tomorrow, Friday. Mr Kasun from Aritzia visits. He will check the leftover trims and the seconds. There is also a J.Crew pre-production meeting. The information security pledge report and the third quarter tax prepayment are due. You also send the weekly cash report and the outsourcing report to Mr Moon.

Saturday, October thirty-first. The fabric and thread count. The truck for the Vince boxes leaves at eight a.m. The ExIm Ledger for September is due from Trinh Do. And the V4 logistics chart is due to head office.
Part six. English review.
Let's review eight expressions. Some are from yesterday. Some are from last week, and four of them you missed on the test, so we will repeat those twice.
The expression is clarify. It means to make something clear. For example, please clarify who enters the lot number, EXIM or the warehouse. Now say it with me.
Please clarify who enters the lot number.
One more time.
Please clarify who enters the lot number.
The expression is mandatory. It means it must be done. For example, the lot number is mandatory for every fabric upload. Now say it with me.
The lot number is mandatory for every fabric upload.
One more time.
The lot number is mandatory for every fabric upload.
The expression is, Is there any way that. We use it to ask for a possible solution politely. For example, is there any way the boxes can be loaded this afternoon? Now say it with me.
Is there any way the boxes can be loaded this afternoon?
One more time.
Is there any way the boxes can be loaded this afternoon?
The expression is expected. It means what we think will happen. For example, please reply with the current status and the expected completion date. Now say it with me.
Please reply with the current status and the expected completion date.
One more time.
Please reply with the current status and the expected completion date.
The expression is, Please update us as soon as. We use it when we need news right away. For example, please update me as soon as the flight is booked. Now say it with me.
Please update me as soon as the flight is booked.
One more time.
Please update me as soon as the flight is booked.
Now the four expressions you missed on the test. Listen carefully.
The expression is outstanding. In business, it means not done yet, or not received yet. It does not mean excellent here. For example, the customs table is still outstanding. Now say it with me.
The customs table is still outstanding.
One more time.
The customs table is still outstanding.
The expression is feasible. It means it can be done in real life. For example, is a Thursday afternoon loading feasible for the packing team? Now say it with me.
Is a Thursday afternoon loading feasible for the packing team?
One more time.
Is a Thursday afternoon loading feasible for the packing team?
The expression is log. As a verb, it means to write down a result or a number. For example, please log the start time and the finish time of the loading. Now say it with me.
Please log the start time and the finish time of the loading.
One more time.
Please log the start time and the finish time of the loading.
The expression is comply with. It means to follow a rule or a standard. For example, the boxes must comply with the new airport size rule. Now say it with me.
The boxes must comply with the new airport size rule.
One more time.
The boxes must comply with the new airport size rule.
Part seven. Role-play.
It is eight thirty in the morning. You walk to the merchandising office and talk to Lency about the Vince boxes.
Anthony says. Good morning, Lency. Did QA finish the pulling test for the broken stitch style?
Lency says. Yes, Mr Lee. They finished yesterday. I will send you the result sheet this morning.
Anthony says. Great. Is the repacking of the one hundred eighty-six pieces done?
Lency says. Almost. The packing team will finish by eleven.
Anthony says. Then what is the expected loading start time?
Lency says. We can start hanging at one thirty this afternoon.
Anthony says. Okay. I will join at one thirty. Please ensure the box sheet and the detail packing list are on the table before we start.
Lency says. No problem. I will bring printed copies.
Anthony says. One more thing. Please log the number of workers, the start time, and the finish time. Last time, I did not get these numbers.
Lency says. Understood. I will send them by email after loading.
Anthony says. Thank you. And Trinh still has no booking confirmation from Hecny. Is there any way you can help her push them?
Lency says. Sure. I will call Hecny with her this morning.
Anthony says. Perfect. Please update me as soon as the booking is confirmed.
Now let's practice two key sentences from this talk.
First sentence. Please ensure the box sheet and the detail packing list are on the table before we start.
One more time.
Please ensure the box sheet and the detail packing list are on the table before we start.
Second sentence. Please log the number of workers, the start time, and the finish time.
One more time.
Please log the number of workers, the start time, and the finish time.
Part eight. Closing.
Here is your one thing for today. Confirm the Vince loading time with Lency first thing, and be on the floor when the boxes are loaded this afternoon.
After that, get the customs table from Trinh Do and report to Mr Moon. Then pick Mr Asanka's flight from Mai's quotes.
You have done the hard part already. The boxes are here, and the questions are clear. Now just follow up, step by step.
Have a good day, Anthony. See you tomorrow, on Friday.
